newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares storm ahead inspired by Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: German shares storm ahead inspired by Dow rally.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse charged ahead on Friday, breaking out of a narrow trading range of recent days, boosted by a sparkling performance overnight on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries.
"The firm dollar, Wall Street and Bunds are all responsible for taking us into the heavens," one dealer said.
The DAX index of 30 top German shares traded up 48.58 points, or 1.73 percent at 2,856.33 points by 1038 GMT.
The DAX had ended bourse trade at 2,807.75 points on Thursday after four days of listless trading, gradually slipping lower in a narrow range.
Dealers said the day's focus would be on the settlement of the DAX December future contract and then later on the expiry of options on constituent DAX stocks.
The said the so-called triple witching joint expiry could help boost the market.

The expiry is called triple witching because market players with expiring futures positions try and square their positions in the cash market on both the index and individual constituent stocks, which can cause price volatility.
Some dealers said the day's rally meant the 2,900 point level was once again in sight for the DAX index for the year-end, but others were more cautious.
Dealers noted out that turnover, as earlier in the week, was not very great and in low volume trade the index could fall as fast as it rose.

Shares in German speciality chemicals group Henkel KGaA were the morning's biggest DAX gainer, after the company said it had received clearance from the German Federal Cartel Office for its pending acquisition of U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp.
The stock was also boosted by news out after Thursday's bourse close that the group plans to acquire the remaining 23 percent of consumer products group Hans Schwarzkopf it does not already own.
Henkel preference shares were up over five percent, or 3.85 marks at 77.45 marks.
